quote: The benchmark assesses LLMs across a range of evaluation categories... requiring the LLM to respond in natural language without hallucination in tools or their parameters.

LLMs need to first hypothesize a tool that is appropriate for the context, and describe the functionality of the tool as well as its parameters. Subsequently, the LLMs retrieve the specified tool and proceed to invoke it according to retrieval results.
outputs: Function calls (JSON format) and natural language responses
function calls in JSON format, tool invocations, and natural language responses in dialogues

quote: We measure the success rate of this meta-tool function calling, which we define as Function Missing Detection (FMD)... We then assess the hit rate of the ground truth tool within the retrieved tool set, denoted as HR@1, HR@3, and HR@5.

We classify all evaluations into three primary groups... Tool Selection Accuracy (T-Acc), which deems a function calling accurate if the invoked tool's name aligns with the ground truth; Parameter Selection Accuracy (P-Acc), where a function calling is accurate only if all parameters of the invoked tool precisely match those of the ground truth... Irrelevance Detection (IRR) serves as a metric to evaluate performance in this regard.

Two straightforward metrics are calculated: (1) Tool Selection Accuracy (T-Acc), which deems a function calling accurate if the invoked tool's name aligns with the ground truth; otherwise, it is marked as inaccurate. (2) Parameter Selection Accuracy (P-Acc), where a function calling is accurate only if all parameters of the invoked tool precisely match those of the ground truth in value.
LLM-based verification utilizes GPT-4o to check for hallucinations, consistency, and adherence to multi-step reasoning
